description: lib.rs:2631: cascade deletion iterates 'd in 2..=leaf_depth' (top-down: shallowest first). When we delete a node at depth d-1 (parent), its children at depth d need deletion too, then grandchildren at d+1, etc. Iterating shallowest-to-deepest is correct only if tree.retain() is called per depth before we move to the next depth. Check this: the code calls tree.retain (line 2641) inside the for d loop, which means at depth d=2 we remove unreachable depth-2 nodes; at d=3 we re-compute reachable from the now-trimmed depth-2 parents. This is correct cascade behavior when done top-down. Confirm and add a comment explaining why top-down iteration is required (bottom-up would miss orphaned nodes when a parent at d=2 is deleted).
title: pkix-path: §6.1.5(g)(iii)(2) cascade-prune for-loop iterates in the wrong direction for child deletion
